analysis.title: DB CoTD: 21 Out of 23 Ain't Bad
key_insights: The S&P 500 rose by less than 1% between the end of May and the end of September 2026.

DB equity strategists Binky Chadha and Parag Thatte find the S&P 500 has risen in 21 of the last 23 midterm election cycles over the window from one month before the election to two months after. The window began this week, with the midterms less than a month away.
The median return over the three-month midterm window is 7%, well above a normal quarterly equity return.
Ahead of most of the historical rallies, markets were fairly flat from mid-July to early October, similar to 2026.

In 1978, equities fell around the midterms as inflation and rates rose. The dollar fell about 8% in October and the Fed raised rates by 100bps to 9.5% on November 1st. The backdrop was more extreme than today's, and the dollar was falling rather than rising.

In 2018, the sell-off had a substantial rates component and trade-war concerns. On October 3rd Powell said the Fed was 'a long way from neutral'. Markets recovered only after Powell turned dovish in the first week of January 2019.
Both exceptions share a rates parallel with today, but neither had an earnings season about to begin with YoY growth expected above 30%.
Q3 earnings season starts next week. DB strategists expect 34% YoY EPS growth, which DB sees as a tailwind for the midterm seasonal pattern even after the recent rates sell-off.
earnings_insights: DB equity strategists (Chadha and Thatte) forecast US Q3 2026 S&P 500 EPS growth of 34% YoY (forecast, season starts next week). Growth is expected to be above 30% YoY.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Historical exception to the midterm seasonal pattern. The rate move was far larger and more urgent than today's.
The dollar was in crisis in 1978. Today the dollar is rising instead.
Expected earnings growth above 30% is a tailwind that neither historical exception had.

risk_factors: The recent rates sell-off could weigh on equities, as in the 1978 and 2018 midterm exceptions.
The 2018 precedent shows a hawkish Fed stance ('a long way from neutral') can override the seasonal pattern until the Fed turns more dovish.
vol_and_positioning: Nervousness remains high in markets despite the seasonally stronger period.
geopolitical: The 2018 sell-off included major concerns about the US-China trade war.

tension_points.bull_case: The S&P 500 rose in 21 of 23 midterm cycles over the window, with a 7% median return, and Q3 EPS growth is expected at 34% YoY.
tension_points.bear_case: The two exceptions (1978 and 2018) both had rate-driven sell-offs, and today has a rates parallel after the recent rates sell-off.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hawkish Fed repricing like the 2018 'a long way from neutral' episode, which kept markets down until Powell turned dovish in January 2019.

theme_stances.key_argument: The S&P 500 has risen in 21 of the last 23 midterm cycles in the window around the election, and strong Q3 earnings should help the pattern reassert itself.
